terminologyProfile.descriptionRule: Use measurable 3D graphics terms. Avoid vague words unless they are paired with concrete geometry/material/shader parameters.

referenceCamera.note: The final authority is the existing project audit camera; reference framing is matched by normalized bounds rather than photo projection.

objectClass.notes: The reference shows one premium stylized apple from a three-quarter view; the companion concept sheet supplies side and near-top evidence. The target is a real-time mobile-game collectible exported as GLB, not a photoreal scan.

reasoning: The fruit body is a continuous sculpt with a five-lobed crown and base, not a scaled sphere.
The thick stem and folded leaf are separately attached silhouette components.
Reference fidelity depends on broad shape, cavity depth, regional color variation, waxy roughness variation, and sparse integrated speckles rather than dense geometry.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Moderate depth is required because the object has only three macro parts but relies on two radial/repeated systems and several localized material/form overrides to avoid reading as a generic red sphere.

detailInventory.note: Enumerate every identity-defining small detail before authoring the spec. Each detail must map to a component.localFeatures entry or material.localOverrides entry, never prose only. Use forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py to scan zones.

details.description: Deep five-way crown cavity around the stem socket
Five broad asymmetric shoulder lobes that interrupt the upper silhouette
Narrower lower third terminating in a soft five-point base indentation
Broad coral-red blush across the lit shoulder and cheek, blended into crimson skin
Broad soft waxy highlight broken by medium roughness, never a hard plastic hotspot
Sparse, low-contrast shallow fruit-skin lenticels integrated into the surface
Thick curved stem with taper, faceted cut top, and restrained vertical wood grain
Leaf with real thickness, central fold, raised vein, and a curled tapered tip

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

definitionOfDone: At the fixed game-like three-quarter camera the apple reads as a premium five-lobed apple, not a sphere or pumpkin.
The top cavity remains clearly recessed, while the lower third tapers into a stable soft five-point base.
The curved stem is visibly embedded in the crown and the folded leaf overlaps its base without a gap.
Neutral and grazing renders show broad waxy highlights, regional crimson-to-coral variation, cavity darkening, and restrained lenticels without plastic glare.
The normalized GLB preserves current physics/loading contracts and stays within a 4k-triangle mobile budget.

featureGroups.name: Five-lobed apple silhouette
qualityCriteria: Width is concentrated around the upper-middle body, the lower third narrows, and five restrained shoulder lobes remain readable without forming a pumpkin.
evidenceRefs: concept sheet side and top views
failureModes: body reads as a smooth sphere
radial lobes are deep enough to read as a pumpkin
bottom remains as wide as the shoulders

featureGroups.name: Crown cavity and five-point base
qualityCriteria: The crown cavity forms a real concave depression around the stem socket and the base ends in a shallow five-point indentation that remains stable on the physics floor.
failureModes: stem emerges from a flat cap
cavity is represented only by dark color
base is flat or terminates in a sharp unstable point

featureGroups.name: Embedded stem and folded leaf assembly
qualityCriteria: The thick curved stem overlaps the crown socket and the leaf overlaps the stem base with visible thickness, central fold, raised vein, and tapered curled tip.
evidenceRefs: hero upper center and upper right
failureModes: stem or leaf floats above the body
leaf reads as a flat oval
stem is a perfectly straight uniform cylinder

featureGroups.name: Waxy fruit skin without plastic glare
qualityCriteria: Crimson base, coral shoulder blush, burgundy cavity darkening, medium roughness variation, broad waxy highlight, and sparse low-contrast lenticels remain independently controllable.
Neutral and grazing light both preserve skin volume without a hard white hotspot.
failureModes: skin is one flat red albedo
speckles read as protruding beads or high-contrast dirt

featureGroups.name: Mobile game-camera readability and budget
qualityCriteria: Crown cavity, one leaf, body taper, and non-spherical silhouette survive the fixed near-top audit camera and icon downsampling.
The GLB stays normalized to maximum dimension 1.0, uses no floating decorative shells, and remains under 4k triangles.
failureModes: improvement appears only in a hero close-up
leaf or cavity disappears at game scale
extra detail exceeds the mobile triangle budget

visualDeltaChecks: old near-sphere silhouette versus new upper-heavy tapered silhouette
old shallow top dent versus new concave five-way crown cavity
old tiny straight stem/leaf versus new embedded curved stem and folded leaf
old flat red material versus crimson-coral-burgundy regional response

visualAcceptance.scoringRule: AI vision must inspect a side-by-side reference/render sheet and score the current pass from 0 to 1. Pixel-diff code may assist diagnostics but cannot approve a pass.

featureReviewPolicy.selectionRule: Choose only the most visually salient, identity-defining, user-prioritized, or high-risk semantic systems. Group repeated parts instead of reviewing every mesh. AI vision scores every selected feature from the same full reference/render pair.

specRefineTriggers: local feature not traceable to viewEvidence
codeRefineTriggers: spec is adequate but generated geometry/material does not match
lighting hides geometry or material response
stopCriteria: target fidelity reached or user accepts current approximation
remaining gaps require new reference images or manual art

screenshotPolicy.minimumEvidence: Each visual pass needs a reference image, rendered screenshot, side-by-side comparison sheet, AI vision score, layer scores, and critique before choosing continue.
screenshotPolicy.reviewPairRule: Compare the same camera/viewpoint whenever possible; do not judge a front reference against a random render angle.
screenshotPolicy.acceptanceAuthority: AI vision review of the comparison sheet. Code-generated pixel similarity is not sufficient evidence.

referencePbrExtraction.acceptedLimitation: single-image extraction is reference-derived inference, not exact photogrammetry

mustAvoid: plastic-looking smooth bark, stone, cloth, foliage, or aged material
local color/detail described only in prose without material masks

screenshotReview: Compare albedo palette and local color zones.
Compare cavity dirt, edge wear, stains, moss, scratches, or other local masks.
Compare key/fill/rim structure, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadows.
Capture a neutral-light render to verify material readability without reference lighting.
Capture a grazing-light close-up to expose flat normals, uniform roughness, tiling, and plastic highlights.
Capture a reference-matched render from the same camera framing as the source.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

buildPasses.goal: Match material color, roughness, bump, and local variation.

buildPasses.goal: Protect runtime performance after visual fidelity is accepted.

lodPlan.strategy: full component tree and material layers
merge static components and reduce local feature geometry

performanceBudget.optimizationPolicy: Preserve silhouette, crown cavity, leaf fold, and waxy material response; simplify only invisible micro relief.

lightingFromPhoto: key light: broad warm-neutral area light from camera upper-left, soft shadow, exposure 0.0 with AgX or ACES-like tone mapping
fill light: cool-neutral low-intensity fill from camera right to retain burgundy cavity separation without flattening the lobes
rim/environment light: restrained warm rear rim plus neutral environment; soft ground contact shadow and ambient occlusion at the stem socket
proceduralStrategy: Create stable pivot groups, sockets, collider proxies, and destruction metadata before visual polish.
Refine forms with bevels, tapers, bends, and procedural noise.
Run reference PBR extraction for important source-image materials and stop when confidence is below the target threshold.
Add material variation before adding expensive micro-geometry.
animationAnchors: root pivot node supports whole-object translation, rotation, scale, and visibility changes
component pivot groups support later local transforms without rebuilding geometry
destructionAnchors: actionProfile.destruction.fractureGroup marks detachable or breakable component sets
component seams and sockets define plausible break points instead of random explosions
risks: Single-image PBR extraction is evidence, not exact inverse rendering; neutral and grazing review remain mandatory.
The concept bottom is partly shadowed, so the five-point base must stay shallow for stable Jolt contact.
Cocos imports GLB materials differently from Blender; the fixed project audit plus runtime screenshot is the final material authority.
